body:
The three inputs agree more than they dispute, and where they dispute the fault lines are locatable. Here is what I use, revise, reject, and leave open, with the grounds where they carry weight.

What converges. All three concede that the material cannot settle the diagnosis; nothing below pretends otherwise. The account's avoid-list — no single big settlement meeting, no moral language about pulling weight, no counting instances in the moment — is contested by no one, and I adopt it unchanged. The consequential convergence is this: the account's strongest observation, by the lights of both other inputs, is the one it treated as secondary — the avoidance may be about the form of the conversations rather than the chores. The objection reaches that by criticizing the account's ordering; the rival reaches it by building an alternative frame. Different routes, same destination, and the destination is the datum the ambiguity hypothesis does not explain. Ambiguity predicts more argument about terms, not absence from the conversation. So the conversational-form question moves to the front — as a question, not a conclusion. The ground for fronting it is explanatory coverage of the one distinctive observation, plus two different lines landing there.

What I use. From the account: the small-scale machinery — two or three most-recurred chores, each specified for done-ness, timing, and fallback; the separate, low-pressure approach to the withdrawn friend; and the threshold at which the question stops being about chores. From the objection: its three-way taxonomy of the same surface observation — ambiguity about what was specified, renegotiation pressure after a schedule change, and a legitimacy question about who may hold whom to terms. That is sharper than the account's own problem note, and I adopt it as the frame. From the rival: two things. First, a genuinely discriminating observation — when a written spec is proposed, does the withdrawn friend engage with its content or pull back from the proposal itself? Second, truce-shaped arrangements (owned zones, unaudited defaults), which I elevate for a reason the rival only half-states: under unresolved diagnosis, they are the arrangement least dependent on which reading is right, because they reduce the number of occasions that require agreement under every reading. Robustness, not accuracy, is their warrant.

What I revise. Three revisions.

First, the order. The account ran chores-first, relationship-later, and the objection is right that this ordering quietly treated the ambiguity reading as already earned. The revision is from serial to parallel: the concrete probe, the form-sensitive conversations, and the observation period all run in the same fortnight.

Second, the test. Falling recurrence cannot confirm the ambiguity hypothesis: friction can fall on specified items while the driver is load or resentment, complaints can migrate to new items, and the next schedule change can bring everything back. I replace the single count with three differential observations. (a) Reaction to the proposal itself, per the rival: content-engagement supports ambiguity; pullback from the idea supports the constitutional reading. (b) Migration: a clean fall fits ambiguity; reappearance of the same dispute on new items fits load or legitimacy. (c) Fallback-use: if the fallback clause is used and accepted, the renegotiation gap was real and is now covered; if the fallback itself becomes the contested thing — why must I announce a day ahead? — then the dispute is about standing, which no specification reaches.

Third, the rival's opener. I do not adopt "ask each flatmate what the flat is" as a first move. Someone withdrawing from chore conversations is likely to read an abstract interview about what the household means as escalation, and the same information comes cheaper attached to a live decision. The revision: pose the constitutional question obliquely, as a real choice — would you rather we each own zones nobody audits, or keep shared standards with a fallback when shifts move? — inside the two separate small conversations, which stay separate and unaggregated. This probes the legitimacy reading at the same time, because standing to enforce within a unit shades into whether there is a unit at all; it is one axis at two depths.

One partial defense of the account before it is revised further: its third column — what happens when someone cannot do it — is already a renegotiation clause, so the objection's claim that the specification move addresses ambiguity alone overstates the miss. The correction is to the account's framing and test, not to its paperwork.

What I reject. Three things. The pretense of neutrality for any arrangement: the rival is right that a written spec enacts the unit-side, but the symmetric risk it flags is real — owned zones enact the privacy-side, and even the choice-question can be felt as a demand. Nothing here is neutral, so whatever emerges gets named as a truce between readings, not as the obviously correct system. Second, single-outcome confirmation: even the cleanest pattern warrants extending the notes gradually, not declaring a hypothesis confirmed. Third, sequencing defended by plausibility alone — which is what distorted the account's order, and which I have tried to design out by making the plan run several hypotheses at once. Not much else is rejected: the objection's self-objection stands, and ambiguity remains the plainest reading of the literal surface. Its demotion is from "the" reading to "a leading" reading, not to a ruled-out one.

What stays open. Everything the three problem-records mark: which reading is right; whether the load is in fact balanced; what the withdrawn friend wants; and whether the avoidance is reasonable — the probes are designed precisely so that this last does not have to be answered first.

The plan, compressed. Week zero: draft revisable three-line notes for the two or three most-recurred chores; hold two ten-minute separate conversations, the withdrawn friend first, offering the zones-or-shared choice as genuine and giving explicit permission to answer that the talks themselves are the problem. Weeks one and two: watch the three observations; count nothing. Then match response to pattern. Engagement plus clean fall: extend the notes gradually. Migration or a contested fallback: open the standing question directly and name it as such. Pullback from the proposal: put owned zones on the table as a first-class option. Zones declined too: open the living-arrangement question — named, not forced from a chore dispute, and not indefinitely deferred. That threshold merges the account's final step with the rival's, and it is the one part of either input I would not soften.
